text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening and final paragraph","quality":"organization","description":"The essay is more clearly structured with an introduction, body paragraphs, and a conclusion that help guide the reader through the argument."},{"evidence":"states \"driverless cars do not seem to take a higher lead\" and \"are not a necessity\"","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"The essay more explicitly presents a position on driverless cars and keeps that position visible throughout."},{"evidence":"\"however, some people might argue\" paragraph","quality":"counterargument","description":"The essay more directly acknowledges an opposing view and responds to it, which makes the argument more persuasive."},{"evidence":"\"if the person took an all nighter... or was having a baby\"","quality":"reasoning","description":"The essay gives fuller explanation for why the technology might matter in certain situations instead of only listing facts."},{"evidence":"references to sensors being used, refined, and still faulty","quality":"use of evidence","description":"The essay uses article details in a more connected way to support its claims rather than mentioning them only briefly."},{"evidence":"repeated claim that cars are \"not completely driverless right now\"","quality":"development","description":"The essay develops its main idea across multiple paragraphs instead of leaving the argument underdeveloped."},{"evidence":"\"driverless cars may not be the thing of the future, but will always be looked upon in the present with awe and glory\"","quality":"conclusion","description":"The essay ends with a more complete concluding statement that restates the stance and wraps up the argument."}]}
